entries.name: AcceptFailure
entries.signature: export type AcceptFailure = (failure: Failure) => void;
entries.jsdocSummary: `ctx.accept` of a command or an effect: marks one refusal that this handler's `write` or `run` returned as handled, so the handler may still return a success. Check the value first, then accept it: `if (OutOfStock.is(r)) { accept(r); ... }`. One call clears one return of that very value. It commits nothing by itself: a returned failure still rolls back. A value the handler never received, a second call for one return, a call after the handler finished, or a value that is not a failure throws `INVALID_ACCEPT`.

entries.name: backoff
entries.signature: export declare const backoff: { /** * Waits `base`, then twice as long before each later retry: `base * 2^(attempt - 1)`, * capped at `max`, varied by `jitter`. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 200, max: 5000, jitter: 0.25 }).upTo(3) */ exponential(options: ExponentialBackoffOptions): Backoff; /** * Waits the same `ms` before every retry. * * @example backoff.constant(60_000).upTo(1) */ constant(ms: number): Backoff; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Builders of a {@link Backoff}. Every builder retries forever until `upTo` limits it.

entries.name: Backoff
entries.signature: export type Backoff = { /** * The wait in milliseconds before retry number `attempt` (1 for the first retry) after * `reason` failed the previous try: the error it threw, or the failure it returned. * `undefined` means stop: do not retry. Throws `InvalidBackoffError` when `attempt` is * not a whole number from 1. */ delay(attempt: number, reason: unknown): number | undefined; /** The most retries this backoff allows: what `upTo` set, or `Infinity`. */ readonly maxRetries: number; /** The same backoff, stopping after at most `retries` retries. `upTo(0)` never retries. */ upTo(retries: number): Backoff; /** * The same backoff, also retrying returned failures of these `@arki/failure` * definitions. Thrown errors keep retrying as without `while`; other returned * failures are not retried. Short for * `while(reason => !isFailure(reason) || definitions.some(d => d.is(reason)))`. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 100 }).while(DbTimeout, ExportUnavailable) */ while(...definitions: RetryableFailures): Backoff; /** * The same backoff, retrying only the reasons for which `predicate` returns true. A * reason is a thrown error or a returned failure, so the predicate sees both: a * returned failure is retried only when a predicate says yes to it. A negative * predicate such as `reason => !(reason instanceof BadInput)` says yes to failures too. * * @example backoff.exponential({ base: 100 }).while(reason => reason instanceof NetworkError) */ while(predicate: RetryPredicate): Backoff; };
entries.jsdocSummary: How long to wait before each retry, and when to stop. Immutable: `upTo` and `while` return a new backoff. Each call narrows the backoff, except that the first `while` decides alone whether a returned failure is retried.

entries.name: BATCH_LIMIT

entries.name: BatchSummary

entries.jsdocSummary: A batch at a glance: how many of its runs are in each state, and their ids, oldest first. `runIds` holds at most `BATCH_LIMIT`; `more` is true when there are more (one id is used by several `startBatch` calls), and `runs(db, { batchId })` pages through all of them.

entries.name: CallOptions
entries.signature: export type CallOptions = { /** * Makes the call idempotent. The first run with this key records its result in * `journal_receipts`, in its own transaction. A later run with the same key and the same * input returns that result without running the handler; the same key with another input * or another command returns `CommandConflict`. The result must survive JSON storage, or the first run * fails with `UNSTABLE_SCHEMA`. Scope a key from outside to its caller: `${tenant}:${id}`. */ readonly idempotencyKey?: string; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options of one call: `journal.run`, a bound runner, a command's `run`, a workflow step's `ctx.run`.

entries.name: combineRunners
entries.signature: export declare function combineRunners<AppDb extends RootDb>(...runners: readonly JobRunner<AppDb>[]): JobRunner<AppDb>;
entries.jsdocSummary: One runner from several, for a worker that runs more than one kind of queue row: `journal.worker(db, { jobs: combineRunners(outboxRunner(...), webhooks.runner) })`. Each row goes to the runner that names its job. Two runners that claim the same name throw `BAD_DEFINITION`: the worker could not tell which one owns the row.

entries.name: Command
entries.signature: export type Command<S extends StandardSchemaV1, R, in MetaOut, in Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, out Writes extends readonly AnyEventDef[] = readonly AnyEventDef[], out Output extends StandardSchemaV1 | undefined = StandardSchemaV1 | undefined> = { readonly name: string; readonly input: S; /** The events this command writes, as declared: readable before boot. A child command's events are its own. */ readonly writes: Writes; /** What a workflow's command node stores of the result. See {@link CommandOptions}. */ readonly output?: Output; /** Bivariant, so a workflow's command node can keep a command in an erased slot and run it without a cast. */ readonly handler: BivariantFn<[input: SchemaOutput<S>, context: CommandContext<MetaOut, Tx, Writes[number]>], R>; /** The command's `authorize` option, when it has one. See {@link CommandOptions}. Its failures are part of `R`. */ readonly authorize?: CommandAuthorize<SchemaOutput<S>, MetaOut, Tx, void | R>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A command: a name, an input schema, the events it writes and a handler. `j.command` makes one; `journal.run` runs it. `name`, `input` and `writes` are for the app (an oRPC procedure can reuse or `.pick` the schema). The handler is for `journal.run` only.

entries.name: COMMAND_FAILURES
entries.signature: export declare const COMMAND_FAILURES: readonly [import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"schema.invalid_input", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<unknown, { issues: readonly import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1.Issue[]; }>>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"schema.async_required", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"schema.validator_defect", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_conflict", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ attempts: number; sqlState: "40001" | "40P01"; }, { attempts: number; sqlState: "40001" | "40P01"; }>>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_unavailable", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_rejected", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ sqlState: string; }, { sqlState: string; }>>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_commit_uncertain", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_cancelled", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"db.transaction_defect", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"contracts.random_source_unavailable", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"failure.unexpected_defect", undefined>, import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.conflict", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ detail: string; }, { detail: string; }>>];
entries.jsdocSummary: Failures owned by command execution, in addition to the command definition's inferred refusals.

entries.name: CommandAuthorize
entries.signature: export type CommandAuthorize<Input, in MetaOut, in Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, Refused = void> = (input: Input, context: { readonly tx: Tx; readonly meta: MetaOut; }) => Refused | Promise<Refused>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Decides whether the caller may run a command. It runs inside the command's transaction, after the input and `meta` are parsed, on every call: a call that replays an idempotency receipt runs it too, before the stored result is returned. Return a failure (`CommandForbidden`, usually) to refuse: the run rolls back, nothing is replayed, and `journal.run` returns that failure. A throw refuses too.

entries.name: CommandConflict
entries.signature: export declare const CommandConflict: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.conflict", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ detail: string; }, { detail: string; }>>; ; export type CommandConflict = ReturnType<typeof CommandConflict>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The current state does not allow it, such as an order that is already paid. See {@link CommandNotFound}. A {@link CommandConflict} failure value.

entries.name: CommandContext
entries.signature: export type CommandContext<out MetaOut, out Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, in Declared extends AnyEventDef = AnyEventDef> = { /** The command's transaction. Use it for reads and for writes outside any entity. */ readonly tx: Tx; /** The parsed metadata every `write` in this command records. */ readonly meta: MetaOut; /** This run's `cmd_` id. Every event it writes carries it. */ readonly commandId: string; /** The chain this run belongs to. Every event it writes carries it; a child run inherits it. */ readonly correlationId: string; /** * `journal.write` on this command's transaction with this command's metadata. Safe to destructure. * A failure `events` returns comes back here: return it from the handler, and the command rolls back. */ readonly write: CommandWrite<MetaOut, Tx, Declared>; /** Run another command in a savepoint of this transaction, with the same metadata. Safe to destructure. */ readonly run: <S extends StandardSchemaV1, R>(command: Command<S, R, MetaOut, Tx>, input: NoInfer<SchemaInput<S>>, opts?: CallOptions) => Promise<Awaited<R> | CommandFailure>; /** * Marks a refusal that `write` or `run` returned as handled, so the handler may still return a * success: `if (OutOfStock.is(r)) { accept(r); ... }`. Without it, a success after a refusal * throws `IGNORED_FAILURE`. Only this command's own check is lifted: a refused child's * savepoint stays rolled back. Safe to destructure. See `AcceptFailure`. */ readonly accept: AcceptFailure; };

entries.name: CommandFailure
entries.signature: export type CommandFailure = ReturnType<(typeof COMMAND_FAILURES)[number]>;

entries.name: CommandForbidden
entries.signature: export declare const CommandForbidden: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.forbidden", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ detail: string; }, { detail: string; }>>; ; export type CommandForbidden = ReturnType<typeof CommandForbidden>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The caller may not do this. See {@link CommandNotFound}. A {@link CommandForbidden} failure value.

entries.name: CommandHookContext
entries.signature: export type CommandHookContext<MetaOut = unknown> = { readonly name: string; readonly input: unknown; readonly meta: MetaOut; readonly commandId: string; readonly correlationId: string; /** The idempotency key of this call, or null. A hook sees a replayed call too: its handler does not run. */ readonly idempotencyKey: string | null; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a command hook sees. Frozen. `input` is the parsed input; a hook may read it, not change it.

entries.name: CommandInvalid
entries.signature: export declare const CommandInvalid: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.invalid", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ detail: string; }, { detail: string; }>>; ; export type CommandInvalid = ReturnType<typeof CommandInvalid>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The request is wrong in a way the input schema cannot see. See {@link CommandNotFound}. A {@link CommandInvalid} failure value.

entries.name: CommandNotFound
entries.signature: export declare const CommandNotFound: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.not_found", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ detail: string; }, { detail: string; }>>; ; export type CommandNotFound = ReturnType<typeof CommandNotFound>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The four failures a command returns when a rule of the app says no. Return one from a command handler, its `authorize`, or the `events` function of a `write`: the command's transaction rolls back, exactly as for a throw, and `journal.run` returns the same failure to the caller. `detail` is the message, written for the client. An app may return its own `defineFailure` values too; any failure rolls the command back. A {@link CommandNotFound} failure value.

entries.name: CommandOptions
entries.signature: export type CommandOptions<Input, MetaOut, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, Refused extends void | undefined | Failure = void, Writes extends readonly AnyEventDef[] = readonly AnyEventDef[], Output extends StandardSchemaV1 | undefined = undefined> = { /** * The events the handler may write. Required: `[]` is a command that only runs child commands. * `write` takes nothing else, and an event that gets past the types fails the run with * `BAD_DEFINITION` before it is stored. */ readonly writes: Writes; /** * What a workflow's command node stores of the handler's result, as `results.<node>`, checked again by `def.read`. * A persisted outcome needs a runtime schema, and TypeScript cannot make one from a handler's return, so a command * that hands a result to a workflow declares it here. Its output must fit the handler's success and survive JSON. * A command node stores `null` for a command without it. `journal.run` does not use it. */ readonly output?: Output; /** * Put the caller's permission check here, not in the handler. A repeat with an idempotency * key does not run the handler, so a check inside it would not run either: the stored result * would go to whoever replays the key. `authorize` runs on the first call and on every replay. */ readonly authorize?: CommandAuthorize<Input, MetaOut, Tx, Refused>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Options of `j.command`.

entries.name: CommandRunner
entries.signature: export type CommandRunner<MetaOut, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle> = CommandContext<MetaOut, Tx>['run'];
entries.jsdocSummary: The type of `context.run`. Use it in app code that passes `run` on, so the generic signature is not repeated there.

entries.name: CommandWrite
entries.signature: export type CommandWrite<out MetaOut, out Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, in Declared extends AnyEventDef = AnyEventDef> = <K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string, Returned extends readonly ((PendingOf<E> & PendingOf<Declared>) | SchemaFailure)[] | Failure>(entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, MetaOut, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>, events: NextEvents<Tbl, E, Tx, Returned>, opts?: WriteOptions) => Promise<WriteResult<Tbl, E, MetaOut, Key> | Extract<Returned, Failure> | SchemaFailure | IdGenerationFailure>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The type of `context.write`. `events` returns events of `entity` that the command declares in `writes`. A helper that takes `write` names what it writes: `CommandWrite<Meta, Tx, typeof OrderPlaced>`, and a command can pass its own `write` only when it declares at least those events. This is an alias with `Declared` annotated because TypeScript erases the type parameters when it compares two instantiations of one function type, and `Declared` sits in a constraint: without the alias nothing compares it.

entries.jsdocSummary: The Drizzle surface the journal needs. Structural: a Drizzle database and a Drizzle transaction both fit. The journal never touches `db.query`, so the app's relations do not matter here.

entries.signature: export type Effect<Meta = unknown, AppDb = RootDb, N extends Needs = NoNeeds> = { readonly name: string; readonly entities: readonly AnyEntity<Meta>[]; readonly types: ReadonlySet<string>; /** What the handlers need on top of `EffectContext`. Empty for an effect that already has its services. */ readonly needs: N; readonly schedule: EffectSchedule<Meta>; /** The same effect with this schedule. `j.effect('mail', order, handlers).withSchedule({ priority: 5 })`. */ withSchedule(schedule: EffectSchedule<Meta>): Effect<Meta, AppDb, N>; /** Resolves with what the handler returned. An effect only reaches out (mail, push, webhooks, outside APIs), so it has no `run`: a command that follows an event is a `j.task` or a `j.workflow` with `startOn`, which checkpoints each step and can undo it.

entries.jsdocSummary: An effect handler also gets one value for each of the effect's needs `N`, under the need's name. `Context` is what else it sees: `EffectContext` for every effect an app writes.

entries.jsdocSummary: What an effect hook sees. Frozen. `attempt` counts from 1.

entries.name: EffectRetention
entries.signature: export type EffectRetention = { readonly completed?: Keep; readonly dead?: Keep; readonly retryableFor?: RetentionAge; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The per-effect (or per queue job name) override.

entries.name: EntityBuilder
entries.signature: export type EntityBuilder<Kind extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, EventDefs extends AnyEventDef, Meta, Key extends string = 'id', CreateResults = never> = OnOnlyEntityBuilder<Kind, Tbl, EventDefs, Meta, Key, CreateResults> & { /** A create reducer receives no row. entries.name: EventDef
entries.signature: export type EventDef<T extends string, S extends StandardSchemaV1> = BivariantFn<[ data: SchemaInput<S> ], Pending<T, SchemaOutput<S>> | SchemaFailure> & { readonly type: T; readonly schema: S; /** * The event's erased form, for `forget`: the same data with the personal parts * removed. entries.name: EventLog

entries.name: EventLogPosition
entries.signature: export type EventLogPosition = string & { readonly [eventLogPositionBrand]: true; };

A store with another order (a commit position, a resume token) uses its own form. `eventLogPositionSchema` in `@arki/journal/zod` is the one way to make one.

entries.name: EventLogReads
entries.signature: export type EventLogReads = { /** One entity's events, oldest first. */ stream(kind: string, entityId: string, filter?: { readonly types?: readonly string[]; readonly afterVersion?: number; readonly limit?: number; }): Promise<readonly StoredEvent[]>; /** The entity's last version, 0 when it has no events. */ highestVersion(kind: string, entityId: string): Promise<number>; /** Only when the log has a global order. entries.name: EventLogWrites
entries.signature: export type EventLogWrites = { /** * Append one entity's events, all or nothing, at versions `expectedVersion + 1` onwards. The * same event ids again is a success that changes nothing. A version already taken by another * event is `JournalError('CONFLICT')`. */ append(batch: { readonly kind: string; readonly entityId: string; readonly expectedVersion: number; readonly events: readonly EventToAppend[]; }): Promise<void>; /** * Only when events can be rewritten in place: replace one event's data and stamp it erased. * Returns the stamp, which a second erase keeps. entries.name: EventOptions
entries.signature: export type EventOptions<S extends StandardSchemaV1, U extends readonly StandardSchemaV1[] = readonly []> = { /** See `EventDef.erased`. */ readonly erased?: (data: SchemaOutput<S>) => SchemaInput<S>; /** * Older shapes of this event, oldest first: `{ from: schemaV1, up: v1 => v2 }`, then * `{ from: schemaV2, up: v2 => v3 }`. The last step's result must fit the current schema. * Append a step when the event's data changes incompatibly; never edit or remove one. */ readonly upcasters?: UpcasterSteps<U>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The third argument of `j.event`.

entries.name: EventsOf
entries.signature: export type EventsOf<E> = E extends { readonly $events?: infer D; } ? Extract<NonNullable<D>, AnyEventDef> : never;
entries.jsdocSummary: The event definitions an entity accepts, read from its phantom `$events`.

entries.name: EventStorage
entries.signature: export type EventStorage = 'stored' | 'transient' | EventLog;
entries.jsdocSummary: Whether and where an entity's events are kept. `'stored'`: every write appends its events to `journal_events`, and replay, verify, repair, forget, rerun, async projections and taps work. `'transient'`: the events exist only inside the write (inline projections, the write's result) and in the effect jobs they queue; nothing reads them back later. An `EventLog`: the events go to that log. One that joins the transaction is written with the row; one that cannot is forwarded: a `forward` job appends them after the commit.

entries.name: EventToAppend
entries.signature: export type EventToAppend = Omit<StoredEvent, 'erasedAt'>;
entries.jsdocSummary: An event to append. `erasedAt` is the log's own, set by `erase`.

entries.name: ForgetResult
entries.signature: export type ForgetResult<Tbl extends EntityTable> = { /** How many events were rewritten in this call. Already-erased events count again: the rewrite is the same. */ readonly erased: number; /** The row after repair from the erased log, or `null` if the log says the entity is gone. */ readonly row: Row<Tbl> | null; };

entries.name: ForwardLag
entries.signature: export type ForwardLag = { readonly pending: number; readonly dead: number; readonly oldestEnqueuedAt: Date | null; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `journal.forwardLag`: forward jobs not yet appended (`dead` of them stopped), and the oldest one's age.

entries.name: initJournal
entries.signature: export declare const initJournal: { (options: InitOptions): JournalDefinitions<StandardSchemaV1<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>>, DbHandle, RootDb>; <Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>>(options: InitOptions & { readonly meta: Meta; }): JournalDefinitions<Meta, DbHandle, RootDb>; } & { tx: <Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx>>() => { create: { (options: InitOptions): JournalDefinitions<StandardSchemaV1<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>>, Tx, RootDb>; <Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>>(options: InitOptions & { readonly meta: Meta; }): JournalDefinitions<Meta, Tx, RootDb>; }; db: <AppDb extends RootDb>() => { create: { (options: InitOptions): JournalDefinitions<StandardSchemaV1<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>>, Tx, AppDb>; <Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>>(options: InitOptions & { readonly meta: Meta; }): JournalDefinitions<Meta, Tx, AppDb>; }; }; }; db: <AppDb extends RootDb>() => { create: { (options: InitOptions): JournalDefinitions<StandardSchemaV1<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>>, DbHandle, AppDb>; <Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>>(options: InitOptions & { readonly meta: Meta; }): JournalDefinitions<Meta, DbHandle, AppDb>; }; tx: <Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx>>() => { create: { (options: InitOptions): JournalDefinitions<StandardSchemaV1<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>>, Tx, AppDb>; <Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>>(options: InitOptions & { readonly meta: Meta; }): JournalDefinitions<Meta, Tx, AppDb>; }; }; }; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `initJournal({ tables, meta })` types `write`'s `tx`, `events`' `{ tx }` and projection handlers with the structural `DbHandle`. `initJournal.tx<AppTx>() .create({ tables, meta })` uses the app's own Drizzle transaction type instead, so repositories typed against it fit. `initJournal.db<AppDb>()` names the app's root database type: effects get it as `ctx.db`, and `drain` and `worker` then need it. Both are type-only steps and chain in either order. `retention` says how long finished jobs are kept, where they go and how often the sweeper runs. It is the one place for it: archive at ack, the job operations, the sweeper, Foreman and workflow timers all read it. Defaults: completed 7 days, dead 90 days. `events` is the journal's default for whether an entity's events are stored (`'stored'`, the default) or only passed through the write (`'transient'`); `j.entity(kind, table, { events })` overrides it per entity. Workflow runs always store their events.

entries.name: Journal
entries.signature: export type Journal<Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, AppDb extends RootDb = RootDb> = { /** * Append events, run reducers, save the row, run projections, queue jobs. All inside `tx`. * A failure `events` returns is the result: the write's savepoint rolled back. */ write<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string, Returned extends readonly (PendingOf<E> | SchemaFailure)[] | Failure>(tx: Tx, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>, input: WriteInput<Tbl, E, Meta, Tx, Returned>): Promise<WriteResult<Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key> | Extract<Returned, Failure> | SchemaFailure | IdGenerationFailure>; /** * Parse `input` and `meta`, then call the command's handler inside one * transaction of `source`. A root database opens a transaction; a transaction * opens a savepoint. Returns what the handler returns. Unexpected callback * exceptions and runtime invariants return typed transaction failures with a private cause. * A returned failure (`@arki/failure`) rolls the transaction back like a throw, and is * returned, the same instance. * On a root database, a run that queued a job calls `wake()` after the commit. */ run<S extends StandardSchemaV1, R>(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, command: Command<S, R, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>, input: NoInfer<SchemaInput<S>>, meta: SchemaInput<Meta>, opts?: RunOptions): Promise<Awaited<R> | CommandFailure>; /** * The command door: `run` with `source` and `meta` fixed. It returns * `(command, input) => journal.run(source, command, input, meta)`. A request * context binds it once with the signed-in actor; a job binds it with a * system actor. The caller still gives `meta`: the library never picks an actor. * `source` follows the rules of `run`: a root database commits and wakes, a * transaction joins and leaves the commit to the caller. * `meta` is parsed on every call, not once here, so a bound runner is exactly * `run`: a default in the meta schema gives each command its own value, and * a bad `meta` rejects the call, inside the transaction guard, as `run` does. */ bind(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, meta: SchemaInput<Meta>, opts?: RunOptions): CommandRunner<SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; /** * Bring a row that existed before the journal into it. The row must be at version 0 * with no history, or `CONFLICT`. `events` builds exactly one create event from the * stored row. Its `.create` reducer must rebuild that row exactly, column by column, * or `VALUE_MISMATCH` and nothing changes: replay folds from nothing and must land on * the row as it is. The event is recorded as version 1 and the row moves to version 1, * so `replay`, `verify` and `repair` work from then on. Projections run and effects * are queued as for any write, because the event is the app's own. */ adopt<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(tx: Tx, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>, input: WriteInput<Tbl, E, Meta, Tx>): Promise<WriteResult<Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key> | SchemaFailure | IdGenerationFailure>; /** Rebuild the row from the log in memory. `throughVersion` is the last version applied. */ replay<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(db: DbHandle, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>, opts?: { readonly throughVersion?: number; }): Promise<ReplayResult<Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key> | SchemaFailure>; /** Replay and compare with the stored row on the columns the reducers produce. */ verify<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(db: DbHandle, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>): Promise<VerifyResult<Tbl, Key> | SchemaFailure>; /** * Remove personal data from one entity's history. Every stored event whose definition * has an `erased` form gets its `data` rewritten to that form and `erased_at` set; events * without one are left alone. Then the row is repaired from the rewritten log, so the row * and its history agree. All in one transaction: an erased form the schema rejects is * `BAD_DEFINITION` and nothing changes; a history replay cannot rebuild (a legacy row that * was never adopted) is `NO_HISTORY` and nothing changes. Projections are not rerun, and no * job is queued: the app owns its read models. Running it twice is safe. */ forget<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(db: DbHandle, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>): Promise<ForgetResult<Tbl> | SchemaFailure>; /** * Delete receipts recorded before `before`. Receipts hold inputs and results, which may * carry personal data; `forget` does not touch them, so an app that keys personal flows * prunes on a schedule. Unresolved HTTP reservations and unexpired HTTP replays are * retained; reconcile unresolved application work before releasing its reservation. * Returns how many were deleted. */ pruneReceipts(db: DbHandle, opts: { readonly before: Date; }): Promise<number | IdGenerationFailure>; /** Lock the row, replay, save the result. Writes no event, runs no projection, creates no job. */ repair<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(db: DbHandle, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, id: EntityId<Tbl, Key>): Promise<Row<Tbl> | null | SchemaFailure>; /** * The async lane of projections: one batch per async projection. Each batch locks the * projection's cursor, scans the next `batchSize` events in commit order, applies the * matching ones on that transaction, and moves the cursor to the last event scanned. * The worker calls it after every drain; call it yourself in tests or one-off scripts. * A projection whose batch throws is skipped this pass and tried again next pass. */ catchUp(db: RootDb & TransactionSource<Tx>, opts?: { readonly batchSize?: number; }): Promise<{ readonly scanned: number; }>; /** * Rewind an async projection to the start. `clear` runs on the same transaction, after the * cursor is locked and before it is rewound, so the read model is emptied and refilled with * no batch landing in between. To rebuild without downtime, deploy the projection under a * new name into a new table instead, wait until `cursors` no longer shows it `behind`, then switch reads. */ reset(db: RootDb & TransactionSource<Tx>, projection: Projection<SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>, clear?: (tx: Tx) => Promise<void>): Promise<void>; /** Per async projection: its position in the log, whether the log holds newer events, and how many positions behind it is when the log can tell. */ cursors(db: DbHandle): Promise<readonly ProjectionCursor[]>; /** * How far the forwarded event logs are behind the rows: forward jobs still waiting or dead, and * when the oldest was written. Effects run from the write's own events, so they may run before * the log has them. */ forwardLag(db: DbHandle): Promise<ForwardLag>; /** * Copy an entity kind's events from the log it uses now into `to` (`'stored'`: the built-in * log), to switch its store. Pause writes to the kind, copy, flip its `events` setting, then * `reset` the async projections that read it: their positions belong to the old log. The old * log keeps its copy. Refused while forward jobs of the kind wait (`FORWARD_PENDING`) and for a * log without a global order. Safe to run again after a crash: appends repeat as no-ops. */ copyLog<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Key extends string>(db: DbHandle, entity: EntityDef<K, Tbl, E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>, opts: { readonly to: 'stored' | EventLog; readonly batchSize?: number; }): Promise<{ readonly events: number; }>; /** Walk the log after position `after` (`null` or left out: from the start) and call one inline projection's handlers, a batch per transaction. Async projections use `reset` and `catchUp`. */ rerun(db: TransactionSource<Tx>, projection: Projection<SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>, opts?: { readonly after?: EventLogPosition | null; readonly batchSize?: number; }): Promise<{ readonly events: number; } | SchemaFailure>; /** * Run up to `batchSize` due jobs. Returns how many jobs were claimed. Root database only. * It must open the journal's transaction type: a workflow step runs commands on it. * Each job is claimed right before it runs, so its lease (`leaseSeconds`, default 60) * covers only its own work, and the lease is renewed every half lease while the effect * runs. A lost lease aborts the effect's `ctx.signal`. * Once `signal` is aborted no further job is claimed; the running one sees it as `ctx.signal`. * `services` and `jobs`: see `worker`. */ drain(db: AppDb & RootDb & TransactionSource<Tx>, opts?: { readonly batchSize?: number; readonly signal?: AbortSignal; readonly leaseSeconds?: number; readonly services?: HandlerServices; readonly jobs?: JobRunner<AppDb>; }): Promise<number | IdGenerationFailure>; /** * A loop around `drain`. The same database as `drain`. `stop()` aborts the running * effect's `ctx.signal`, claims nothing more, and resolves when that effect returns. */ worker(db: AppDb & RootDb & TransactionSource<Tx>, opts?: { readonly pollMs?: number; readonly batchSize?: number; readonly leaseSeconds?: number; /** * Hear the wake channel (`journal.wakeChannel`): a commit that recorded events wakes this * worker at once, from any process, and the journal's taps fire here for those events. * Required when the journal has taps, unless `taps: false` says this worker runs jobs only. */ readonly listen?: WakeListener; /** `false`: a jobs-only worker in a journal that has taps. Another process must listen. */ readonly taps?: boolean; /** * The services of a journal composed with `services: 'worker'`, per effect and tap. * A need without a value throws here, before the worker starts. A journal composed * with its services ignores this. */ readonly services?: HandlerServices; /** * Runs `kind = 'queue'` rows (jobs scheduled by `@arki/queue/outbox`) whose name is in * `jobs.names`, under the same lease and fenced ack as effects. Without it the worker * claims effect rows only, exactly as before. */ readonly jobs?: JobRunner<AppDb>; }): JournalWorker; /** * The Postgres channel every commit that recorded events notifies, with the seq range as * JSON `{ "from": n, "to": m }`. `journal_wake`, or `<schema>_journal_wake` for tables in a * schema. Payloads are small and bounded; a listener loads what it needs by seq. */ readonly wakeChannel: string; /** * Wake every running worker this journal started in this process. Call it * after committing a transaction of your own that ran commands. No worker: nothing happens. */ wake(): void; /** * Pending jobs no handler can claim, counted per kind and name: effect rows whose effect * this journal does not have and, given the worker's `jobs` runner, queue rows whose name * it does not know. Without `jobs`, queue rows are not counted. * `drain` leaves them alone, because during a rolling deploy an older worker may * still have that handler. After the deploy, a non-empty list means a handler was * renamed or removed while it had jobs: bring it back under its old name until * the count is zero, or delete those job rows on purpose. */ strandedJobs(db: DbHandle, opts?: { readonly jobs?: Pick<JobRunner, 'names'>; }): Promise<readonly StrandedJobs[]>; /** * The resolved archive policy: the `retention` option of `initJournal` with its defaults filled in. The one source the * worker, the verbs and the sweeper read. */ readonly retention: ResolvedRetention; /** * List jobs: `pending` (the default) is everything not dead, oldest due first; `dead` is what the worker * gave up on, newest first. `state` says where each is now. `limit` 1 to 200, default 100. `next` is the cursor * of the following page (pass it as `after`), null on the last. `effect` filters effect rows, `job` queue rows. */ jobs: JobOps['jobs']; /** One job with its event header, its attempts (`attemptLog`) and the latest operations that touched it. */ job: JobOps['job']; /** Per effect and queue job name: how many jobs are ready, delayed, running and dead. */ jobCounts: JobOps['jobCounts']; /** Who did what to the jobs, newest first. `jobId` keeps the operations that touched one job. */ jobOperations: JobOps['jobOperations']; /** Finished jobs, newest first, with `outcome`, `effect` and `job` filters. */ archivedJobs: JobOps['archivedJobs']; /** One finished job with its attempt log, or undefined. */ archivedJob: JobOps['archivedJob']; /** How many archive rows there are, how many wait for the sink, and how many are past `keepUntil`. */ archiveStatus: JobOps['archiveStatus']; /** * Workflow runs, read and operated on: `runs`, `run`, `counts`, `stranded`, `history`, and the operator verbs * `retryStep`, `resolveStep`, `skipUndo`, `signal`, `cancel` and `checkResult`. The verbs need * `compose({ workflows, workflowMeta })`. */ readonly workflows: WorkflowOps<Tx>; /** * The limits the registered workflows hold (`concurrency`), read and changed at runtime: `list`, `get`, and the * operator verbs `override`, `reset`, `pause` and `resume`. The verbs need `compose({ workflows, workflowMeta })`. */ readonly limits: LimitOps<Tx>; /** A dead job back to pending: attempts and lease cleared, due now, workers woken. `JOB_NOT_DEAD` otherwise. */ retry: JobOps['retry']; /** A dead job leaves the hot table, archived as `discarded`. `JOB_NOT_DEAD` otherwise. */ discard: JobOps['discard']; /** A ready or delayed job leaves the hot table, archived as `cancelled`. `JOB_RUNNING` or `JOB_NOT_PENDING` otherwise. */ cancel: JobOps['cancel']; /** Retry many dead jobs by ids or by filter, all or none by ids. `operationId` is null when nothing matched. */ retryDead: JobOps['retryDead']; /** Dead jobs older than `olderThan` leave the hot table, archived or deleted by the retention policy. */ purgeDead: JobOps['purgeDead']; /** * Send unexported archive rows to `retention.archive.sink`, oldest first, up to `limit`. Marks them exported only * after the sink resolved (at-least-once); a throwing sink leaves them and returns `failed: true`. No sink: a no-op. * `op` defaults to the actor `system:retention`. */ exportArchive: JobOps['exportArchive']; /** * Delete archive rows past `keep_until` and the oldest beyond any `max`. With a sink, only exported rows go. * `op` defaults to the actor `system:retention`. */ pruneArchive: JobOps['pruneArchive']; /** * Delete finished workflow runs past their `keep_until`, with their steps and signals. The events stay. A run is never * pruned while it or an ancestor is unfinished. `op` defaults to the actor `system:retention`. */ pruneWorkflows: JobOps['pruneWorkflows']; /** Delete operation rows past the `operations` keep. Writes no operation row of its own. */ pruneOperations: JobOps['pruneOperations']; /** A new job from an archived one. Not a retry: it gets a new id. `JOB_EXISTS` when a live job holds the dedupe key. Not `replay`, which rebuilds an entity from its events. */ replayJob: JobOps['replayJob']; /** * The one way to extend a run from outside: a wrapper that receives the context and * `next`. Command hooks run inside the transaction, around the handler; effect hooks run * inside the lease, around the handler. Rules: call `next` exactly once, or throw before * it to stop; a rejection of `next` is the hook's rejection too; the context is frozen * and the result cannot be changed; hooks run in registration order, the first outermost. * Register at boot: once the journal has run a command, a drain or a worker, `around` * throws `BAD_DEFINITION`. Step hooks wrap each workflow step body and undo, inside the * `journal.step` span; they are frozen by the first drain or worker. */ readonly hooks: { readonly command: HookPoint<CommandHookContext<SchemaOutput<Meta>>>; readonly effect: HookPoint<EffectHookContext<SchemaOutput<Meta>>>; readonly step: HookPoint<StepHookContext>; }; readonly catalog: { /** * Only the entities that a projection or an effect of this journal names. An * entity that no handler names is not listed, even when the app writes to it. */ readonly entities: readonly EntityInfo[]; readonly projections: readonly string[]; readonly effects: readonly string[]; readonly taps: readonly string[]; }; };

entries.name: JournalDefinitions
entries.signature: export type JournalDefinitions<Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle, AppDb extends RootDb = RootDb> = { /** * An event. `schema` and each upcaster's `from` are Standard Schemas, parsed sync * (`parse`) by the constructor, `write` and replay. */ event<T extends string, S extends StandardSchemaV1, const U extends readonly StandardSchemaV1[] = readonly []>(type: T, schema: S, opts?: EventOptions<S, U>): EventDef<T, S>; /** * The key column is `id`. `options.events` says whether this entity's events are stored * (`'stored'`) or only passed through the write (`'transient'`); it overrides the journal's * `events` default. A transient entity has no history: replay, verify, repair, forget, rerun, * adopt, async projections and taps are refused for it. */ entity<K extends string, Tbl extends IdTable>(kind: K, table: Tbl, options?: { readonly events?: EventStorage; }): EntityBuilder<K, Tbl, never, SchemaOutput<Meta>, 'id'>; /** * The key column is the one `table` holds under the property name `options.key`: * a non-null string column that is the primary key or unique. */ entity<K extends string, Tbl extends EntityTable, Key extends KeyName<Tbl>>(kind: K, table: Tbl, options: { readonly key: Key & SingleKey<Key>; readonly events?: EventStorage; }): EntityBuilder<K, Tbl, never, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Key>; /** * A command: `input` (any Standard Schema) is parsed async (`parseAsync`) before * the handler runs, like the command's `meta`; the handler's * `write` and `run` are bound to one transaction and one parsed `meta`. * `options.writes` lists the events the handler writes, and `write` takes nothing else. * `options.output` is what a workflow's command node stores of the result. * Needs only `j`, entities and events, never the finished journal. */ command<S extends StandardSchemaV1, R, const Writes extends readonly AnyEventDef[], Refused extends void | undefined | Failure = void, Output extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Resolved<R>> | undefined = undefined>(name: string, input: S, options: CommandOptions<SchemaOutput<S>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx, Refused, Writes, Output>, handler: (input: SchemaOutput<S>, context: CommandContext<SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx, Writes[number]>) => R): Command<S, R | Extract<Refused, Failure>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx, Writes, Output>; /** `on` is `NoInfer` so `E` comes from `entity`; handlers are then contextually typed. */ projection<E extends AnyEntity<SchemaOutput<Meta>>>(name: string, entity: E | readonly E[], on: NoInfer<ProjectionHandlers<E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>>, opts?: ProjectionOptions): Projection<SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; effect<E extends AnyEntity<SchemaOutput<Meta>>>(name: string, entity: E | readonly E[], on: NoInfer<EffectHandlers<E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb>>): Effect<SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb>; /** * An effect that needs a service: `needs` is `{ mailer: need<Mailer>() }`, and each * handler then gets `mailer` in its context, next to `jobId`, `attempt`, `signal` and `db`. * An effect has no `run`: a command that follows an event is a `j.task` or a `j.workflow` with `startOn`. */ effect<E extends AnyEntity<SchemaOutput<Meta>>, N extends Needs>(name: string, entity: E | readonly E[], needs: N, on: NoInfer<EffectHandlers<E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb, N>>): Effect<SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb, N>; /** * Build the runtime journal from the tables given to `initJournal` and the handlers. `services` holds one * value for every need of every listed effect, by name. A need without a value throws here, unless `services` is `'worker'`. * `const`: the list is read as a tuple, so an effect with needs keeps them next to one without. */ /** A tap: in-process, after commit, lossy. See `Tap`. Same shapes as `effect`. */ tap<E extends AnyEntity<SchemaOutput<Meta>>>(name: string, entity: E | readonly E[], on: NoInfer<TapHandlers<E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb>>): Tap<SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb>; tap<E extends AnyEntity<SchemaOutput<Meta>>, N extends Needs>(name: string, entity: E | readonly E[], needs: N, on: NoInfer<TapHandlers<E, SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb, N>>): Tap<SchemaOutput<Meta>, AppDb, N>; /** * A limit several workflows share: list it in each one's `concurrency.shared`. `total` caps the unfinished runs that * hold it, `perKey` those with one concurrency key; at least one, each a positive whole number. Throws * `BAD_DEFINITION` otherwise, and for a name that starts with `workflow/` (a workflow's own limit). */ limit(def: LimitDef): LimitDef; /** * A durable workflow: `.step(...)` nodes, then `.finish()`. The finished definition has `start`, a command: * `context.run(refund.start, { input, id? })` returns `{ runId }` (a repeat with the same `id` and input returns the * same run; another input is a `CommandConflict`). entries.name: JournalTables
entries.signature: export type JournalTables = ReturnType<typeof journalTables>;

entries.name: JournalWorker
entries.signature: export type JournalWorker = { start(): Promise<void>; stop(): Promise<void>; wake(): void; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `wake()` runs a drain pass now instead of at the next poll. It does nothing unless the worker is running.

entries.name: Keep
entries.signature: export type Keep = false | 'forever' | 'untilExported' | RetentionAge | { readonly age: RetentionAge | 'forever'; readonly max?: number; };

The job is deleted the moment it finishes. - `'forever'`: kept until someone deletes it. - `'untilExported'`: kept only until the archive sink has it, then deleted. entries.name: KeyColumn
entries.signature: export type KeyColumn = AnyPgColumn<{ data: string; notNull: true; }>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A column that can hold an entity's key: a non-null string column.

entries.name: LifecycleHookContext
entries.signature: export type LifecycleHookContext<Input, Ending, N extends Needs = NoNeeds, AppDb = RootDb, Run = unknown> = Needed<N> & Ending & { readonly runId: string; readonly workflow: string; readonly version: number; readonly scope: string | null; readonly tags: readonly string[]; readonly metadata: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; readonly input: Input; readonly jobId: string; /** 1 on the hook job's first try, 2 on its next, and so on. */ readonly attempt: number; readonly signal: AbortSignal; readonly db: AppDb; readonly run: Run; readonly accept: AcceptFailure; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a lifecycle hook sees: the run that ended (`runId`, `workflow`, `version`, `scope`, `tags`, `metadata`, the typed `input`, and how it ended), the context of the hook's job (`db`, `run`, `accept`, `signal`, `jobId`, `attempt`), and the definition's needs by name, as a step gets them. `run` without a meta records the app's `workflowMeta`, as in a step. `metadata` is the run's metadata as it ended: the run is over, so a hook reads it and cannot change it.

entries.name: LifecycleHooks
entries.signature: export type LifecycleHooks<Input, Output, N extends Needs = NoNeeds, AppDb = RootDb, Run = unknown> = { /** The run completed. `ctx.output` is its output. */ success?(ctx: LifecycleHookContext<Input, EndingIn<Output, 'completed'>, N, AppDb, Run>): unknown; /** The run failed. `ctx.error` is the text of its error, as `RunFailed` recorded it. */ failure?(ctx: LifecycleHookContext<Input, EndingIn<Output, 'failed'>, N, AppDb, Run>): unknown; /** The run was cancelled, after any undo it had to do. */ cancel?(ctx: LifecycleHookContext<Input, EndingIn<Output, 'cancelled'>, N, AppDb, Run>): unknown; /** The run's `ttl` passed before its first node started, so nothing ran. */ expired?(ctx: LifecycleHookContext<Input, EndingIn<Output, 'expired'>, N, AppDb, Run>): unknown; /** Every end, after the specific hook, or alone. `ctx.state` says which end. */ complete?(ctx: LifecycleHookContext<Input, RunEnding<Output>, N, AppDb, Run>): unknown; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `on`: what runs when a run ends. Hooks are durable, not callbacks: the end of a run queues one job (the `workflow.on` effect) in the transaction that ends it, so a hook runs only after that commit, and at least once. The job runs the hooks of the run's own version: the specific one, then `complete`. A throw is retried as an effect's is; a returned failure is final. The run has ended: no hook changes its state. Method signatures, so a typed `on` fits the erased one a definition keeps; see `BivariantFn`.

entries.name: LIMIT_BOUNDS
entries.signature: export declare const LIMIT_BOUNDS: { readonly name: 128; readonly shared: 2; readonly runningShown: 100; readonly promoteTries: 50; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The bounds of limits: a `j.limit` name is at most 128 characters, a workflow lists at most 2 shared limits (as trigger.dev does), and `WorkflowBusy.running` names at most 100 runs. When a slot frees, at most `promoteTries` queued runs are checked, oldest first, so a run end or an operator verb does a bounded amount of work.

entries.name: LIMIT_BUSY_REASONS
entries.signature: export declare const LIMIT_BUSY_REASONS: readonly ['full', 'paused'];
entries.jsdocSummary: Why a limit refuses a start (`WorkflowBusy.reason`): it is `full`, or an operator `paused` it.

entries.name: LIMIT_KEY_TTL
entries.signature: export declare const LIMIT_KEY_TTL: { readonly default: '7d'; readonly max: '30d'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: How long a `perKey` override of one key lasts: 7 days unless `ttl` says otherwise, and at most 30 days.

entries.name: LimitBusyReason
entries.signature: export type LimitBusyReason = (typeof LIMIT_BUSY_REASONS)[number];
entries.jsdocSummary: Why a limit refuses a start: it is `full`, or an operator `paused` it.

entries.name: LimitDef
entries.signature: export type LimitDef = { readonly name: string; readonly total?: number | undefined; readonly perKey?: number | undefined; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A limit several workflows share: `total` caps the unfinished runs that hold it, `perKey` those that hold it with one concurrency key (the `key` of each workflow's `concurrency`). At least one of the two, each a positive whole number.

entries.name: LimitKeyView
entries.signature: export type LimitKeyView = { readonly key: string; } & LimitKeyOverride;
entries.jsdocSummary: A `perKey` override of one key, as `journal.limits` shows it.

entries.name: LimitNameArgs
entries.signature: export type LimitNameArgs = { readonly name: string; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `pause` and `resume` name the limit.

entries.name: LimitOps
entries.signature: export type LimitOps<Tx> = { /** Every limit the registered workflows hold, by name. */ list(db: DbHandle): Promise<LimitView[]>; get(db: DbHandle, name: string): Promise<LimitView | CommandNotFound>; /** * Replaces a code value until `reset`, or the `perKey` of one key until it expires. `CommandInvalid` for a value * that cannot apply: any override of a workflow without `concurrency`, or a `perKey` where no start has a key. */ override(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: LimitOverrideArgs, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<LimitView | CommandNotFound | CommandInvalid | CommandFailure>; /** The code values again: of one key, or without `key` of the whole limit. entries.jsdocSummary: `journal.limits`: what limits there are and the operator verbs that change them. Each verb writes one event on the `journal.limit` entity, which carries `op.actor`, `op.reason` and `op.executionId`, and returns the limit after it. An unknown name is `CommandNotFound`.

entries.name: LimitOverrideArgs
entries.signature: export type LimitOverrideArgs = { readonly name: string; readonly key: string; readonly perKey: number; readonly ttl?: RetentionAge | undefined; } | { readonly name: string; readonly total?: number | undefined; readonly perKey?: number | undefined; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `override` sets the `perKey` of one key for `ttl` (default `LIMIT_KEY_TTL.default`, at most `.max`), or the limit's own `total` and `perKey` (at least one) until `reset`. 0 admits no run: `perKey: 0` blocks a key.

entries.name: LimitResetArgs
entries.signature: export type LimitResetArgs = { readonly name: string; readonly key?: string | undefined; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `reset` drops the override of one key, or without `key` every override of the limit (not its pause).

entries.name: LimitValues
entries.signature: export type LimitValues = { readonly total: number | null; readonly perKey: number | null; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A limit's `total` and `perKey`; null for none.

entries.name: LimitView
entries.signature: export type LimitView = { readonly name: string; readonly workflows: readonly string[]; readonly code: LimitValues; /** The `total` and `perKey` an operator set, which replace the code values until `reset`. */ readonly override: LimitValues; /** The `perKey` overrides of single keys that have not expired. */ readonly keys: readonly LimitKeyView[]; /** The values a start is checked against: an override, or else the code value. entries.jsdocSummary: One limit as `journal.limits` shows it: the code values, what an operator changed, and what applies now.

entries.name: MetadataChange
entries.signature: export type MetadataChange = { readonly kind: 'set'; readonly patch: RunMetadata; } | { readonly kind: 'increment'; readonly key: string; readonly by: number; } | { readonly kind: 'append'; readonly key: string; readonly value: unknown; } | { readonly kind: 'remove'; readonly key: string; };
entries.jsdocSummary: One change to a run's metadata after its start: what `ctx.metadata` and `journal.workflows.setMetadata` make, one `MetadataChanged` event each. `set` merges `patch` into the top level, `increment` adds `by` to a number (a missing key counts as 0), `append` pushes `value` onto an array (a missing key starts one), `remove` drops a key.

entries.name: MetadataContext
entries.signature: export type MetadataContext = { /** Merges `patch` into the top level of the metadata. */ set(patch: RunMetadata): Promise<MetadataOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** Adds `by` (default 1) to the number at `key`. A missing key counts as 0. */ increment(key: string, by?: number): Promise<MetadataOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** Pushes `value` onto the array at `key`. A missing key starts an array. */ append(key: string, value: unknown): Promise<MetadataOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** Drops `key`. A missing key is no change. */ remove(key: string): Promise<MetadataOutcome | CommandFailure>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `ctx.metadata` in a step or undo body. Each call is one command and one `MetadataChanged` event on the run, committed at once, so a reader sees it while the step still runs. A refusal is the value the call returns (`CommandConflict` once the run has finished, `CommandInvalid` for a wrong type or metadata over the limit); it never fails the step. A retried attempt runs its calls again: `set` and `remove` give the same metadata, `increment` and `append` apply once more per attempt.

entries.name: MetadataOutcome
entries.signature: export type MetadataOutcome = { readonly metadata: RunMetadata; } | CommandNotFound | CommandConflict | CommandInvalid;
entries.jsdocSummary: What a metadata change returns: the run's metadata after it, or why it was refused. `CommandNotFound`: no such run. `CommandConflict`: the run has finished. `CommandInvalid`: a wrong value type, or metadata over the limit.

entries.name: ndjsonArchiveSink
entries.signature: export declare function ndjsonArchiveSink(options: ArchiveObjectStore & { /** Default `journal-archive`. */ readonly prefix?: string; }): ArchiveSink;
entries.jsdocSummary: An {@link ArchiveSink} that writes one NDJSON file per batch: one JSON line per archived job, in batch order. The key is `<prefix>/YYYY/MM/DD/<first archived_at in ms>-<first id>.ndjson` (UTC). Resending a batch after a crash between write and mark gives the same key when the batch starts at the same row, so a store that overwrites by key makes the retry harmless; a different start gives another file and the reader dedupes on `id`.

entries.name: need
entries.signature: export declare const need: <T>() => Need<T>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Declare one thing an effect needs: `j.effect('order-mail', order, { mailer: need<Mailer>() }, { ... })`.

entries.name: Need
entries.signature: export type Need<T> = { readonly [needType]?: T; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A marker for one thing an effect needs, such as a mailer. `need<Mailer>()` makes one. It holds the type only. The real value comes later: from `services` in `j.compose`, or from the services of the Dot feature that lists the effect.

entries.name: Needed
entries.signature: export type Needed<N extends Needs> = { readonly [K in keyof N]: N[K] extends Need<infer T> ? T : never; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What the handlers get for the needs `N`: one value per name.

entries.name: Needs
entries.signature: export type Needs = Readonly<Record<string, Need<unknown>>>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The needs of one effect, by the name its handlers read them under.

entries.name: NextEvents
entries.signature: export type NextEvents<Tbl extends EntityTable, E extends AnyEventDef, Tx = DbHandle, Returned extends readonly (PendingOf<E> | SchemaFailure)[] | Failure = readonly (PendingOf<E> | SchemaFailure)[]> = (row: Row<Tbl> | null, ctx: { readonly tx: Tx; }) => Returned | Promise<Returned>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Looks at the locked row, checks the rules, and returns the events to append. Runs after the row is locked, inside the write's savepoint. `tx` is that savepoint: reads through it see the locked row's transaction. Return a failure (`@arki/failure`) when a rule says no: the savepoint rolls back, nothing is written, and the write returns that failure.

entries.name: Patch
entries.signature: export type Patch<Tbl extends EntityTable, Key extends string = 'id'> = Partial<ReducerValues<Tbl, Key>>;

entries.name: Pending
entries.signature: export type Pending<T extends string = string, Data = unknown> = { readonly type: T; readonly data: Data; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A validated event that has not been written yet.

entries.name: PendingOf

entries.jsdocSummary: Options of `journal.run` and `journal.bind`.

entries.name: RunOverrides
entries.signature: export type RunOverrides = { readonly maxAttempts?: number | undefined; readonly timeout?: RetentionAge | undefined; readonly priority?: number | undefined; };
entries.jsdocSummary: How a run's steps run, set at its start and kept for its whole life. `maxAttempts` caps the tries of each step, `timeout` caps each step attempt (an age), and `priority` orders the run's step and timer jobs among due jobs: higher first, the scale of an effect's `priority`. A step's retry and timeout are code, so a run can only narrow them. A child run takes none: it runs as its definition says.

entries.name: RunRetention
entries.signature: export type RunRetention = { /** Default `'7d'`. */ readonly completed?: Keep; /** Default `'90d'`. */ readonly failed?: Keep; /** Default: the `failed` value. */ readonly cancelled?: Keep; /** A run whose `ttl` passed before it started. entries.jsdocSummary: How long a finished workflow run's row is kept, by how it ended. Values are {@link Keep}s, with two limits that `BAD_DEFINITION` enforces: `'untilExported'` (a run has no sink) and `max` (there is no per-name row cap for runs). `false` deletes the run row at the next sweep. A run's events are never pruned.

entries.name: RunState
entries.signature: export type RunState = RunRow['state'];

entries.name: RunSummary
entries.signature: export type RunSummary = Pick<RunRow, 'id' | 'name' | 'workflowVersion' | 'state' | 'node' | 'waitingFor' | 'wakeAt' | 'deadlineAt' | 'parentId' | 'parentPath' | 'scope' | 'tags' | 'rootId' | 'batchId' | 'replayOf' | 'cancelledAt' | 'cancelReason' | 'startAt' | 'ttlAt' | 'maxAttempts' | 'stepTimeoutMs' | 'priority' | 'startedAt' | 'finishedAt'> & { /** When a delayed run's first node is due, while that is still ahead and it has not started; otherwise null. */ readonly delayedUntil: Date | null; /** A step of this unfinished run is dead and waits for an operator: a failed `undo`, or a failed `do` while the run is not compensating. */ readonly stuck: boolean; /** The run's code is missing or has other nodes. Null for a finished run and for a run with its code. */ readonly stranded: StrandedReason | null; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A run in a list: without its input, results, output and metadata, which can be large.

entries.name: ScheduledJob
entries.signature: export type ScheduledJob = { /** `job_xxx`. Stable across retries: pass it on as an idempotency key. */ readonly id: string; /** The persisted job name, e.g. `'discovery:run'`. */ readonly name: string; readonly args: unknown; /** 1 on the first try. */ readonly attempt: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: One `kind = 'queue'` row as the worker hands it to a runner. `args` is the stored JSON, not yet parsed.

entries.name: Services
entries.signature: export type Services = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Real services by name, as an app or a Dot feature hands them over.

entries.name: ServicesFor

entries.jsdocSummary: Every need of every effect in a list, as one object of services. Two effects that use the same name get the same service. `unknown` when no effect needs anything.

entries.name: StartBatchOutcome
entries.signature: export type StartBatchOutcome = { readonly batchId: string; readonly runs: readonly StartOutcome[]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What `def.startBatch` returns: the batch id, and for each item, in order, what its own `def.start` would have returned.

entries.name: StepHookContext
entries.signature: export type StepHookContext = { readonly workflow: string; readonly version: number; readonly runId: string; /** The node's name. */ readonly step: string; /** 1 on the step's first try, 2 on its next, and so on. */ readonly attempt: number; readonly phase: StepPhase; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a step hook sees: which run, which node, which try, and whether the body (`do`) or the undo runs. Frozen. The run's input and the step's results stay out, as they do from the `journal.step` span.

entries.name: StepView
entries.signature: export type StepView = Pick<StepRow, 'path' | 'phase' | 'attempt' | 'key' | 'jobId' | 'result' | 'error' | 'reason' | 'startedAt' | 'finishedAt'> & { /** `running` while the step's job holds a live lease; otherwise what the row stores. */ readonly status: StepStatus; readonly stuck: boolean; };

entries.name: StoredEvent
entries.signature: export type StoredEvent = JournalTables['events']['$inferSelect'];
entries.jsdocSummary: An event as a log stores and returns it: the `journal_events` row shape.

entries.name: StrandedJobs
entries.signature: export type StrandedJobs = { readonly kind: JobKind; readonly name: string; readonly jobs: number; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Pending jobs no handler of this worker can claim, per kind and name: an effect this journal does not have, or a queue job the runner does not know.

entries.name: StrandedReason
entries.signature: export type StrandedReason = WorkflowStranded['data']['reason'];
entries.jsdocSummary: Why a run has no code to go on with: no registered workflow has its name and version, or the registered one has other nodes.

entries.name: StrandedRun
entries.signature: export type StrandedRun = Pick<RunRow, 'id' | 'name' | 'workflowVersion' | 'state' | 'startedAt'> & { readonly code: StrandedReason; };

entries.name: TagsContext
entries.signature: export type TagsContext = { /** Adds tags the run does not have yet. More than `RUN_FIELD_LIMITS.tags` in all is `CommandInvalid`. */ add(...tags: string[]): Promise<TagsOutcome | CommandFailure>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: `ctx.tags` in a step or undo body: one command and one `RunTagged` event per call that adds a tag, like `ctx.metadata`.

entries.name: TagsOutcome
entries.signature: export type TagsOutcome = { readonly tags: readonly string[]; } | CommandNotFound | CommandConflict | CommandInvalid;
entries.jsdocSummary: What adding tags returns: all the run's tags after it, or the refusal, as for `MetadataOutcome` (over the limit).

entries.name: Tap

It fires in every process whose worker listens on the wake channel, from the seq range the commit announced. For a live page, a cache, a metric. Never for work that must happen: that is an effect.

entries.name: TapContext
entries.signature: export type TapContext<AppDb = RootDb> = { readonly db: AppDb; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a tap handler gets: the root database, plus its needs. No `run`: a tap may not issue commands.

entries.name: TapHandlers
entries.signature: export type TapHandlers<E, Meta, AppDb = RootDb, N extends Needs = NoNeeds> = { readonly [D in EventsOf<E> as D['type']]?: BivariantFn<[ event: RecordedOf<D, Meta, EntityIdOf<E>>, ctx: TapContext<AppDb> & Needed<N> ], unknown>; };

entries.name: TransactionSource
entries.signature: export type TransactionSource<Tx> = { transaction<T>(run: (tx: Tx) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; } & DbHandle;
entries.jsdocSummary: A database or transaction whose nested transactions have type `Tx`. The app's Drizzle transaction type fits `TransactionSource<itself>`: a savepoint has the same type as its parent. The root database fits `TransactionSource<AppTx>`. `DbHandle` fits `TransactionSource<DbHandle>`, which is the default everywhere.

entries.name: Unlisten
entries.signature: export type Unlisten = () => void | Promise<void>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Stops listening. May be async.

entries.name: Upcaster
entries.signature: export type Upcaster = { readonly from: StandardSchemaV1; up(data: unknown): unknown; };
entries.jsdocSummary: One step of an event's history: the schema its data had at one version, and how to lift that data to the next. Replay parses with `from` first, so `up` sees valid old data. `up` is a method signature, so a typed step is an `Upcaster`; see `BivariantFn`.

entries.name: UpcasterSteps
entries.signature: export type UpcasterSteps<U extends readonly StandardSchemaV1[]> = { readonly [K in keyof U]: { readonly from: U[K]; readonly up: (data: SchemaOutput<U[K]>) => unknown; }; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Typed upcaster steps: each `up` receives the output of its own `from`.

entries.name: VerifyResult
entries.signature: export type VerifyResult<Tbl extends EntityTable, Key extends string = 'id'> = { readonly ok: true; } | { readonly ok: false; readonly expected: ReducerRow<Tbl, Key> | null; readonly actual: Row<Tbl> | null; };

entries.name: WakeListener
entries.signature: export type WakeListener = (onMessage: (payload: string) => void) => Unlisten | Promise<Unlisten>;
entries.jsdocSummary: How a worker hears the wake channel. The app wires its own client: for `pg`, a dedicated client that runs `LISTEN <channel>` and calls `onMessage(payload)` on each notification; for PGlite, `client.listen(channel, onMessage)`. Start it before `worker.start()` resolves work you care about: `LISTEN` only hears what is sent after it ran, and the worker still polls.

entries.name: WORKFLOW_LIMIT_PREFIX
entries.signature: export declare const WORKFLOW_LIMIT_PREFIX = "workflow/";
entries.jsdocSummary: The name of a workflow's own limit is this prefix and the workflow name. A `j.limit` name may not start with it.

entries.name: WorkflowBusy
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowBusy: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_busy", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ name: string; key: string | null; limit: number; running: string[]; limitName?: string | undefined; reason?: "full" | "paused" | undefined; detail: string; }, { name: string; key: string | null; limit: number; running: string[]; limitName?: string | undefined; reason?: "full" | "paused" | undefined; detail: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowBusy = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowBusy>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A start found a limit it holds full or paused (`reason`). `limitName` names it: `workflow/<name>` for the workflow's own `concurrency.limit` and `total`, else a `j.limit`. `limit` is the count that is reached (0 for a pause), `key` the start's concurrency key (`null` without one: only a `total` can block such a start). `running` lists the runs of the caller's own scope that hold the limit, oldest first, at most 100; another scope's run ids are never shown. Returned when `onBusy` is `'refuse'`, for a pause, for a full limit other than the workflow's own `perKey`, and always for a child run: a child cannot join a run that another parent started. A {@link WorkflowBusy} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowCommandRunner
entries.signature: export type WorkflowCommandRunner<Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx> = DbHandle> = RootRunnerWith<Meta, Tx, [meta?: SchemaInput<Meta>, opts?: CallOptions]>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The type of `ctx.run` in a workflow body (a step, an undo, a `when`, a `key`, a `next`, a child's `input`). `meta` may be left out: the command then records the `workflowMeta` the app passed to `compose({ workflows, workflowMeta })`. The library still never invents an actor: the app chose `workflowMeta`. A meta passed here is used as given.

entries.name: WorkflowDef
entries.signature: export type WorkflowDef<Input extends StandardSchemaV1 = StandardSchemaV1, Output = unknown, Signals extends AnySignals = AnySignals, N extends Needs = Needs, ReadOutput = unknown, ReadResults extends AnyResults = AnyResults> = { readonly name: string; readonly version: number; readonly shape: WorkflowShape; readonly shapeHash: string; readonly input: Input; /** The declared output schema, if any. */ readonly output: StandardSchemaV1 | undefined; readonly deadline: RetentionAge | undefined; readonly concurrency: { readonly key: BivariantFn<[input: unknown], string> | undefined; readonly limit: number | undefined; readonly total: number | undefined; readonly shared: readonly LimitDef[]; readonly onBusy: (typeof ON_BUSY)[number]; } | undefined; readonly onDeadStep: 'wait' | 'compensate'; /** The workflow's own run retention; a field left out takes the journal's (`retention.workflows`). */ readonly retention: RunRetention; readonly limits: WorkflowLimits; readonly needs: Needs; /** The journal event that starts a run, if any. entries.jsdocSummary: The finished definition. `types` is a phantom: it carries the output type and the signals, and holds no value. `Signals` defaults to any signal map, so a bare `WorkflowDef` accepts every definition.

entries.name: WorkflowOps
entries.signature: export type WorkflowOps<Tx> = WorkflowReads & WorkflowVerbs<Tx>;

entries.name: WorkflowPending
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowPending: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_pending", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; }, { runId: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowPending = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowPending>;
entries.jsdocSummary: `def.settled` or `def.startAndWait` stopped waiting before the run ended. The run goes on: a wait never cancels it. `runId` is the run to read again later (`def.settled`), or to cancel on purpose. A {@link WorkflowPending} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowReadMismatch
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowReadMismatch: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_read_mismatch", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; field: string; detail: string; }, { runId: string; field: string; detail: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowReadMismatch = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowReadMismatch>;
entries.jsdocSummary: What `def.read` returns when a stored value of the run does not fit its schema. `field` is `input`, `output` or `results.<node>`; `detail` is the `WORKFLOW_READ_MISMATCH` message, and the cause is the schema's `InvalidInput`, with its issues. A {@link WorkflowReadMismatch} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowReads
entries.signature: export type WorkflowReads = { /** Runs, newest first, with an opaque `next` cursor (pass it as `after`). `limit` 1 to 200, default 100. */ runs(db: DbHandle, opts?: RunFilter & PageOptions): Promise<{ readonly runs: RunSummary[]; readonly next: string | null; }>; /** One run with its steps, children and unconsumed signals; undefined when there is no such run. */ run(db: DbHandle, id: string): Promise<RunDetail | undefined>; /** How many runs there are per workflow name, version and state. */ counts(db: DbHandle): Promise<RunCount[]>; /** The runs of one batch: counts by state and the run ids.
