entries.name: WorkflowRunCancelled
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowRunCancelled: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_run_cancelled", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; reason: string | null; }, { runId: string; reason: string | null; }>>; ; export type WorkflowRunCancelled = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowRunCancelled>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A run that `def.startAndWait` waited for was cancelled. `reason` is the cancel's reason, or `null` when none was recorded. A {@link WorkflowRunCancelled} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowRunFailed
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowRunFailed: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_run_failed", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; state: "expired" | "failed"; error: string; }, { runId: string; state: "expired" | "failed"; error: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowRunFailed = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowRunFailed>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A run that `def.startAndWait` waited for ended `failed` (or `expired`): a step died, or a node refused. `error` is the text the run recorded. A {@link WorkflowRunFailed} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowShape
entries.signature: export type WorkflowShape = { readonly nodes: readonly { readonly name: string; readonly kind: 'step' | 'waitFor' | 'eventWait' | 'sleep' | 'child' | 'map' | 'command' | 'parallel'; readonly undo: boolean; /** A child node's choice when its parent cancels or compensates; only on `child` nodes. */ readonly onCancel?: 'cancel' | 'detach'; /** The signal a `waitFor` node waits for; only on `waitFor` nodes. */ readonly signal?: string; /** The name of the command a `command` node runs; only on `command` nodes. */ readonly command?: string; /** The name of the command that undoes a `command` node; only on one with an `undo`. */ readonly undoCommand?: string; /** What an `eventWait` node waits for: each label with its entity kind and event types. Part of the shape hash. */ readonly on?: readonly { readonly label: string; readonly entity: string; readonly events: readonly string[]; }[]; /** How a `parallel` node ends: when every branch completed, or when the first did. Part of the shape hash. */ readonly wait?: 'all' | 'any'; /** The branches of a `parallel` node, each with the nodes of its own definition. Part of the shape hash. */ readonly branches?: readonly { readonly name: string; readonly shape: WorkflowShape; }[]; }[]; };
entries.jsdocSummary: The node manifest a run pins at start: names, kinds, order, and which nodes have an undo. Stored in `workflow_runs.shape` so Foreman can draw a stranded run whose code is gone. Plain JSON; the builder (step 2) produces it.

entries.name: WorkflowStarter
entries.signature: export type WorkflowStarter<Meta extends StandardSchemaV1<unknown, Record<string, unknown>>, Tx extends TransactionSource<Tx>, Input extends StandardSchemaV1, Signals extends AnySignals, ReadOutput, ReadResults> = { readonly start: Command<StartSchema<Input>, Promise<StartOutcome | CommandFailure>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; /** * The command that starts many runs in one transaction, all with one `batchId`. Each item is the arguments of * `start`, and `runs[i]` is item i's outcome: a refused item (`WorkflowBusy`, `CommandConflict`, ...) rolls back * only its own savepoint. An item that does not fit the start schema refuses the whole batch with `InvalidInput`. */ readonly startBatch: Command<StartBatchSchema<Input>, Promise<StartBatchOutcome | CommandFailure>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; /** * The command that delivers the signal `name` to a run. `name` is one of the signals the workflow's `waitFor` * nodes declare, and `payload` is the input of that signal's schema. */ readonly signal: <Name extends keyof Signals & string>(name: Name) => Command<SignalSchema<Signals[Name]>, Promise<SignalOutcome | CommandFailure>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; /** The command that cancels a run: it stops, undoes its completed steps newest first, and ends `cancelled`. */ readonly cancel: Command<CancelSchema, Promise<CancelOutcome | CommandFailure>, SchemaOutput<Meta>, Tx>; /** * One run of this workflow, as `journal.workflows.run` reads it, typed by the definition. `undefined` when there is * no such run, or the run belongs to another workflow. * * Values with a schema are checked when read, and typed by that schema: the input; the output when the workflow * declares an `output` schema (`null` until the run completes); the result of each step with an `output` schema * (the schema's output, not what the step returned) and of each `waitFor`. Any other result is `unknown`, and a * node that has not run is missing. A run whose stored values no longer fit * returns `WORKFLOW_READ_MISMATCH` (failure code `journal.workflow_read_mismatch`); read it untyped with * `journal.workflows.run`. A run started on an older version is checked the same way. * * The stored input is the input schema's output, so a schema whose output is not a valid input (a transform) * makes `read` refuse. */ readonly read: (db: DbHandle, runId: string) => Promise<ReadOutcome<SchemaOutput<Input>, ReadOutput, ReadResults>>; /** * The typed run (as `read` gives it) once it has ended, or `WorkflowPending { runId }` when `within` seconds pass * first. `within` is required, above 0 and at most 30. It polls the run with a growing pause; waiting never changes * the run. It needs the root database: a transaction handle throws `BAD_ARGUMENT`, because a wait inside a * transaction holds it open and a snapshot would never see the run end. */ readonly settled: (db: RootDb, runId: string, options: SettleOptions) => Promise<SettledOutcome<SchemaOutput<Input>, ReadOutput, ReadResults>>; /** * Starts a run (`start`) and waits for it to end, for a caller that must answer with the result, such as a request. * Root database only (a transaction handle throws `BAD_ARGUMENT`). A timeout or an abort never cancels the run: the * result is `WorkflowPending { runId }`, and the caller can take the id and read it later. The workflow must be * registered with `compose({ workflows })`, which gives it the journal to start with. */ readonly startAndWait: (db: RootDb & TransactionSource<Tx>, args: StartArgs<SchemaInput<Input>>, options: StartAndWaitOptions<SchemaInput<Meta>>) => Promise<StartAndWaitOutcome<ReadOutput>>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: What a journal adds to a finished definition.

entries.name: WorkflowStranded
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowStranded: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_stranded", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; name: string; version: number; reason: "WORKFLOW_SHAPE_CHANGED" | "WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN"; detail: string; }, { runId: string; name: string; version: number; reason: "WORKFLOW_SHAPE_CHANGED" | "WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN"; detail: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowStranded = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowStranded>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The pinned workflow code is unavailable or incompatible; keep the run unchanged until an operator restores it.

entries.name: WorkflowTransitionLimit
entries.signature: export declare const WorkflowTransitionLimit: import("@arki/failure").FailureDefinition<"journal.workflow_transition_limit", import("@standard-schema/spec").StandardSchemaV1<{ runId: string; name: string; limit: number; transitions: number; detail: string; }, { runId: string; name: string; limit: number; transitions: number; detail: string; }>>; ; export type WorkflowTransitionLimit = ReturnType<typeof WorkflowTransitionLimit>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A run tried to start a node past its workflow's `limits.transitions`, so it stops: it compensates, then ends `failed` with this failure as its error. `limit` is the workflow's `limits.transitions`; `transitions` is the count the run had reached. A transition is the first try of a node: each visit of a node in a loop counts, and so does a node its `when` skips; a retry and an undo do not. A {@link WorkflowTransitionLimit} failure value.

entries.name: WorkflowVerbs
entries.signature: export type WorkflowVerbs<Tx> = { /** * A dead step runs again. A failed `do` or `undo` step gets its next attempt with the same key. A failed child or map * node starts its failed children again under new ids (`<id>~2`, then `~3`); the old runs stay as history. When the * run is stranded, every dead job of the run (steps, parks, deadline, undos) is retried once the code is registered * again, each with the job verb's operations row and a `JobRetried` event; until then the stranded error is thrown. * `STEP_NOT_DEAD` for any other step. */ retryStep(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly path: string; readonly phase: StepPhase; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<{ readonly how: 'rescheduled' | 'childrenRestarted' | 'jobRetried'; } | CommandFailure>; /** * Gives the result of a failed `do` step of a running run. Compensation goes on and the path is `residual`. */ skipUndo(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly path: string; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<{ readonly runId: string; } | CommandFailure>; /** * Delivers signal `name` to a run, for an operator who holds only JSON: the run's own version checks the payload * (`def.signal(name)` is the typed door for app code; both are one transition). A repeated `deliveryId` is a * `duplicate`. `SignalReceived` carries the operator. */ signal(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly name: string; readonly deliveryId: string; readonly payload: unknown; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<SignalOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** Cancels a run of any workflow, for an operator: the same transition as `def.cancel`. `CancelRequested` carries the operator. */ cancel(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly reason: string; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<CancelOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** * Changes the metadata of an unfinished run (running, parked or compensating), like `ctx.metadata` in a step: one * `MetadataChange` (`set`, `increment`, `append` or `remove`) and one `MetadataChanged` event, which carries the * operator. `CommandConflict` once the run has finished; `CommandInvalid` for a wrong value type or metadata over the * limit. Returns the metadata after the change. */ setMetadata(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly change: MetadataChange; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<MetadataOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** * Adds tags to an unfinished run, like `ctx.tags.add`: tags it has already change nothing, the rest go in one * `RunTagged` event that carries the operator. `CommandInvalid` past `RUN_FIELD_LIMITS.tags`. Returns all its tags. */ addTags(source: TransactionSource<Tx>, args: { readonly runId: string; readonly tags: readonly string[]; }, op: JobOperationInput): Promise<TagsOutcome | CommandFailure>; /** * Whether `resolveStep` would take `result` for step `path`: the step's `output` schema of the run's own version * checks it, and nothing is written. A step `resolveStep` could never resolve throws `STEP_NOT_RESOLVABLE`. */ /** * Moves the start of a run whose first node has not started: its first node becomes due at the new time (a time in * the past is now), and its `ttl` and deadline count from it. entries.name: postgresEvents
entries.signature: export declare function postgresEvents(deps: { readonly db: DbHandle; readonly tables: EventLogTables; }): ForwardedLog;
entries.jsdocSummary: Events here are appended by many workers at once, and the app's seq is stamped before the append, so neither seq nor commit time is an order a reader can follow safely. The order is `(transaction_id, seq)`, read only below the oldest transaction still open (the snapshot's `xmin`). Every transaction below it has ended, and every later one gets a higher id, so no row can ever commit behind what a read returned. Cost: one long transaction anywhere on that Postgres server holds async projections back until it ends.
